messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager — GPU autoscaler alert for cluster-prod-eu-west-1. GPU inference queue > 1.8k, sustained 3m. Autoscaler attempted 3 scaleups but nodes not joining. Paging on-call.

Maria G: acked. I'm on it, grabbing diagnostics. First glance: autoscaler shows failures to create/attach instances and launch template errors.

Samir K: hitting this now too. stack traces in the autoscaler logs show a mix of attach timeout + permission errors. copying snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T02:14:31Z ERROR autoscaler: autoscaler: failed to create instance: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
status code: 403, request id: b1234-xxxx
2026-03-15T02:14:33Z WARN autoscaler: ASG attach timed out (attach timeout 120s) -> cleanup
```

Ira P: aws console -> the ASG attempted to launch, EC2 starts then terminates with InstanceLifecycle: spot, reason: LaunchTemplate referencing invalid iam instance profile.

Alex R: Confirmed: recent change to launch-template LT-20260314 replaced instance profile to new name "redwood-gpu-ephemeral" but role policy missing iam:PassRole for the cluster-autoscaler instance IAM. That would explain AccessDenied during instance creation.

Maria G: ok. mitigation plan: 1) temp scale up a spare, non-tainted GPU nodegroup (gpu-fallback-01) to drain queue, 2) patch launch template permissions / add correct instance-profile, 3) let autoscaler try again, 4) fallback routing for critical customers to smaller model instances. Who can scale ASG manually?

Samir K: I can. I'm going to set desired capacity +3 on the fallback ASG (gpu-fallback-01) and set max to +5. Using AWS console now. Will also create a temporary nodegroup via eksctl if ASG scaling doesn't finish.

DevOps Bot: command run by Samir K: aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-fallback-01 --desired-capacity 3 --honor-cooldown false :white_check_mark:

Samir K: ASG changed to desired 3, new instances are provisioning. Waiting for node registration.

Maria G: I'm preparing a short-term routing rule in router to send 10% of traffic from tier:free -> smaller model variant to reduce burst while we recover. Ira, can you coordinate with Customer Ops on impacted tenants?

Ira P: pinging Customer Ops... @Customer Ops — we see elevated 5xxs and high latency for some tenants using large-generation routes (gpt-large-gpu). Affected: customers with sustained batch jobs and some hosted chat sessions. We'll send a brief status update.

Customer Ops: Received. Drafting status: "We are experiencing degraded generation latency due to GPU capacity exhaustion; mitigation in progress (temporary scaling + fallback models). No data loss, some requests may be delayed or served at lower model quality." Will post in 10m.

Alex R: autoscaler logs now showing LaunchTemplate validation error fixed after I applied iam:PassRole to the instance profile and reattached the profile to LT-20260314. Command used (aws UI + iam update): 
```
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name redwood-autoscaler-role --policy-name AllowPassRole --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"iam:PassRole","Resource":"arn:aws:iam::*:role/redwood-instance-role"}]}'
```

Maria G: great. After that, autoscaler retried and attempted scaleups. One problem left: the new nodegroup templates include a taint gpu=exclusive:NoSchedule which our inference pods don't tolerate (they rely on tolerations that were supposed to be applied by the daemonset but missed on rollout). I'm going to temporarily remove the taint from new nodes to let pods schedule.

Samir K: I can remove the taint on newly joined nodes via kubectl once they are Ready. Run sequence: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l nodegroup=gpu-fallback-01 -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl taint nodes {} gpu=exclusive:NoSchedule-
```

DevOps Bot: nodes gpu-fallback-01-i-0a1b2c ready and taint removed.

Samir K: pods are scheduling onto new GPUs. Queue length down from 1872 -> 842 in 6 minutes. Good sign.

Maria G: I'm going to flip the router rule now to reduce fallback to 5% and ramp model routing back gradually. Monitoring p99 latency and 5xx.

Ira P: Customer Ops posted status update. No major escalations yet, one enterprise customer asked for dedicated capacity — sales already looped in.

Alex R: autoscaler now performing additional scaleups successfully. I see events: 
- 1832468002: ASG gpu-prod-2 increased desiredCapacity from 45 -> 48
- 1832468120: new node i-0fae... joined kubelet and registered with taints gpu=exclusive:NoSchedule (we removed them)

Samir K: queue now 220 and dropping. Throttled: some requests were retried once by inference layer. No lost requests, but higher latency spikes during window.

Maria G: marking incident as mitigated for customer-impacting behavior. Continuing to watch for 15m. Next actions for postmortem: 
- root cause: launch template IAM change + missing iam:PassRole -> prevented new EC2 from being fully provisioned.
- secondary: rollout omitted toleration config in inference daemonset causing taint mismatch on new nodes.
- remediation tasks: add CI check to validate LT IAM role policies before promotion; add autoscaler health check to fail open with clearer reason if iam:PassRole denied; ensure daemonset rollout includes tolerations as part of release checklist.

DevOps Bot: incident state updated -> mitigated by on-call.

Alex R: I'm going to open a PR for the LT validation and another to add an autoscaler error classifier to raise a structured alert when instance creation is AccessDenied.

Customer Ops: Posted final customer-facing note: "Issue mitigated — GPU capacity restored; some requests may have experienced delays. Engineering investigating root cause; follow-up expected."

Maria G: Thanks everyone. Handing off to Samir for monitoring + postmortem. @Samir K — please own the follow-up doc + timeline.

Samir K: will do, creating incident-1832467890 postmortem doc and adding a timeline + actions. Leaving thread open until postmortem link posted.

IncidentBot: Pager cleared by Maria G at 1832468290.

Maria G: closing thread after postmortem published. Great response team. :tada:
